source.check: returned unopposed: no contests (Belfast News-Letter, 18 May 1955, p. 8); 'Mr. Cecil J. Burrowes, J.P., was re-elected vice-chairman' at the new council's first meeting, where M'Ilgorm, Nimmons and Morrow were the co-opted members (Mid-Ulster Mail, 18 June 1955, p. 2, image read); re-elected vice-chairman again after the 1958 election (Belfast Telegraph, 12 June 1958, p. 1)

note: Triennial election of the 19 electoral divisions of Dungannon rural district, one member each. Nominations closed on 17 May 1955 and there were no contests: '13 Unionists and six Nationalists were returned unopposed' (Belfast News-Letter, 18 May 1955, p. 8). No poll was held; Tyrone's polling day was Thursday 2 June 1955. At the new council's first meeting Mr. M. Busby was re-elected chairman and Hugh M'Ilgorm, John Nimmons and Samuel Morrow were co-opted (Mid-Ulster Mail, 18 June 1955, p. 2). Council-meeting method: division inferred from the 5 June 1952 return (Bush: Cecil Burrows, in place of H. A. M'Minn, Belfast News-Letter, 21 May 1952, p. 4); the Mid-Ulster Mail, 18 June 1955, p. 2 names Mr. Cecil J. Burrowes, J.P., as re-elected vice-chairman of the new council, not co-opted; he was vice-chairman again in June 1958. Returned unopposed.
